name: Studielink

jurisdiction.authority: Studielink, on behalf of the Dutch higher education institutions

coverage.includes: Publicly funded research universities and universities of applied sciences.
coverage.excludes: Some institutions handle applicants from abroad through their own systems instead, and private institutions are outside it. Check with the institution before assuming Studielink is the route.

choiceRules.note: The limit of two applies to numerus fixus programmes specifically, and only one may be used where the programme is medicine, dentistry, dental hygiene, physiotherapy or midwifery. Non-selective programmes are not rationed in the same way, and choices are not ranked against each other as they are in Denmark — each application is decided on its own.

identityRequirement: A DigiD, the Dutch digital identity, which the government says takes about five days to obtain. This is the step most likely to catch out an applicant living outside the Netherlands.
decisionModel: Two different things happen depending on the programme. A non-selective programme admits anyone holding a qualifying diploma, which is an entitlement rather than a competition. A numerus fixus programme runs a selection between 15 January and 15 April on criteria the institution sets itself, and issues each applicant a ranking number on 15 April.
replyModel: An offered place must be accepted through Studielink within two weeks, or it passes automatically to the next-ranked applicant. That is a short window, and it falls months before IB results.
